Optimize every important page for:
* SEO titles and meta descriptions * H1, H2, and H3 headings * Primary and secondary keywords * URLs/slugs * Image file names and alt text * Internal linking * Anchor text * Breadcrumbs where appropriate
Make sure each page has a clear SEO focus and unique metadata.

* XML sitemap * Robots.txt * Indexing and crawlability * Canonical URLs * Redirects and broken links * Duplicate content * Mobile usability * Website speed * Core Web Vitals * Image optimization * Plugins and unnecessary scripts * Schema/structured data * WordPress SEO settings
Review Google Search Console if access is provided and correct applicable issues.
## 5. Create 4 New State-Specific Pages

* Florida * Georgia * North Carolina * Texas
Each page should include:

item.title: Advance AI Direct Sales Platform Development (based in Dubai, UAE)

3000-5000 USD | Debrok, an AI-powered direct sales platform for property developers
Debrok gives real estate developers in the UAE a direct-to-buyer sales channel that runs alongside their existing broker network. An AI layer qualifies buyers and investors, hands warm leads to the developer's own sales team, then independently tracks each lead through to close. Buyers use it free of charge. Developers pay.
What we need built:
1. Three portals: Buyer, Developer and Admin.
2. Property data engine. Developers manually enter and maintain projects and units (price, location, unit type and size, payment plan milestones, handover date, availability status). Data is stored in structured fields and queried live by the AI during conversations.
3. AI voice and chat qualification. The AI answers buyer questions using live property data and captures budget, purchase intent (investor vs. end-use), timeline and preferred unit type. Every call is recorded and transcribed, and each conversation produces a structured lead summary. Arabic and English support is required.

5. Post-handoff follow-up. The AI keeps checking in with the buyer after handoff, independently of what the developer reports, to confirm deal status. Cadence is tiered by deal value: higher-value leads get longer, more persistent follow-up and milestone questions (agreement signed, deposit paid). Lower-value leads lapse to "unresponsive" faster. Stalled or evasive high-value leads escalate to a human.
6. Developer reporting. Detailed periodic reports covering leads, conversion and commission statements, plus regional benchmarking that shows each developer how they rank against others on the platform, with the underlying data anonymised.
7. Billing engine. Billing works either/or per month. In a month with no closed deal, the developer pays a flat monthly fee. In a month with a closed deal, the fee is replaced by a 2% commission on the unit value. There must be admin controls for waivers and fee adjustments to support an onboarding phase.
8. Admin portal covering developer management, AI conversation oversight, billing, disputes and platform-wide reporting.
We are asking for a quote based on the above, plus a proposed technical architecture (stack, hosting, voice AI vendor and LLM approach), a phased delivery plan, and a rough estimate of ongoing per-call AI costs.

item.title: Kaspa Credential Verification Blockchain MVP Build
item.description:
250-750 USD | What are we building?
A programmable lifecycle infrastructure layer for physical assets, built on Kaspa.
The goal is to give physical assets a digital identity and verifiable lifecycle, while allowing predefined rules to control how the asset can move from one state to another.
How it works
Physical Asset ↓ Digital Identity ↓ Lifecycle States ↓ Authorized Transitions ↓ Kaspa
For example:
Manufactured → Certified → Sold → Shipped → Delivered → Serviced → Resold → Retired
A business could connect its existing ERP/API and map its existing events to these lifecycle states.
What problem does it solve?
Today, asset information is often fragmented across manufacturers, distributors, logistics companies, service providers and customers.
This can create problems with:
* Authenticity * Ownership verification * Supply-chain visibility * Warranty/service history * Asset transfers * Duplicate records * End-of-life tracking
The platform would create a shared, verifiable lifecycle layer without requiring companies to replace their existing systems.
Why Kaspa?
Kaspa’s UTXO architecture and covenant capabilities can potentially allow important asset-state transitions to become programmable and enforceable, rather than simply being entries in a centralized database.
First MVP
Build one working asset lifecycle to prove the concept:
Create → Certify → Transfer → Deliver → Verify
The MVP would include:
* Digital asset identity * Lifecycle/state engine * Authorized transitions * Kaspa integration * Basic covenant implementation * API integration * Public verification * Simple dashboard
Long-term potential
The same infrastructure could eventually support: Manufacturing Diamonds & jewellery Supply chain Invoice/asset financing Batteries Energy assets Credentials
The vision:
Don’t just record what happened.
Make the next state programmable.
Community initiative
The idea is to build the MVP with the Kaspa community — developers, builders, testers and supporters — using voluntary community donations to fund development.
Development milestones, progress and spending would be made transparent to the community.

While the words are being refined, the visual skin of the site must also come up to modern standards. I want a fresh, contemporary look, seamless mobile responsiveness, and an intuitive flow that makes it obvious where to click next—no hunting, no clutter.
